displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that psychophysical harmony provides modest comparative support for purposive theism when treated as a structured conjunction of consciousness, normative salience, and generally adaptive functional organization, not as a bare correlation.

novelty.explanation: It narrows and restructures the participant's case to preserve a role-level datum despite the identity objection.

premises.text: The relevant evidence is not merely that phenomenal and neural descriptions co-refer, but that valenced experiences, practical reasons, learning dispositions, and behavior form a broadly value-enabling organization.

novelty.explanation: It develops the original value and pain examples into a more explicit multilevel evidential conjunction.

premises.text: Identity theory can remove two independently existing events without explaining why the single event has phenomenal, normative, and functional descriptions that cooperate in this particular value-producing pattern.

novelty.explanation: It answers the identity diagnosis by relocating the explanatory question from numerical correlation to organized roles.

premises.text: A perfectly good creator has a general reason to favor worlds where conscious agents can recognize harms, learn from experience, deliberate responsively, and pursue goods, although that reason does not uniquely determine every detail.

novelty.explanation: It supplies explicit value-enabling functions while limiting the inference so divine goodness does not uniquely predict one world.

premises.text: Comparative support need not rest on a uniform prior over every conceivable mapping if independently describable structural features make the observed conjunction less arbitrary under purposive agency than under an unspecified mapping.

novelty.explanation: It replaces an ignorance-derived measure with a qualified structural comparison responsive to Oppy's strongest objection.

premises.text: The evidential claim should remain conditional on a substantive epistemic gap and should weaken substantially for reductive theories that independently derive valence, function, and rational significance from physical organization.

novelty.explanation: It incorporates Cutter's concession and Oppy's crosscutting point into the scope of the strengthened case.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, psychophysical harmony may provide limited comparative evidence for purposive theism over naturalistic packages that leave the structured value-enabling conjunction unexplained, while providing little evidence against reductive packages that derive it.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion narrows the motion-level claim to explicitly specified theory packages and a modest evidential effect.

newArguments.title: Robustness across representational levels
newArguments.text: The evidential target can be tested for robustness across descriptions. Harmful stimulation, unpleasant phenomenology, avoidance learning, practical reasoning, and protective behavior are independently characterizable, yet normally converge. A purposive hypothesis has a direct reason to favor that convergence because it supports agency and welfare. A naturalistic rival gains parity only by deriving the convergence from independently motivated physical or functional principles. This avoids counting imagined mappings and instead compares how competing complete theories explain one multiply describable organization.

novelty.explanation: This is a new robustness-based evidential strategy that does not depend on a measure over all conceivable psychophysical mappings.

newArguments.title: Conditional explanatory partition
newArguments.text: Partition naturalism into packages that derive harmony and packages that merely posit it. Against the first group, the harmony argument has little force because reduction supplies an internal explanation. Against the second, the coordinated presence of consciousness, valence, reasons, and adaptive function remains an additional structured fact. Theism should likewise be partitioned by its account of divine reasons and embodiment. Evidence can then shift only between matched packages whose auxiliary commitments are explicit, answering the demand for complete-theory comparison while retaining a local evidential role for harmony.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the broad worldview comparison by constructing an explicit package-sensitive comparison framework.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that psychophysical harmony does not presently favor theism because its description, modal alternatives, and probability basis vary with the complete consciousness theory, while identity-based naturalism offers a serious nonselective account.

novelty.explanation: It combines Oppy's ontological, probabilistic, and methodological replies into one proportionate negative thesis.

premises.text: Evidence must be specified consistently across hypotheses, yet bare phenomenal-neural coinstantiation, normative-functional alignment, and value-producing agency are different data with different explanatory requirements.

novelty.explanation: It corrects the overly broad probability-one claim by separating several possible formulations of harmony.

premises.text: On a reductive identity account, phenomenal character and physical organization are not independently selected variables, so many imagined remappings are not alternatives admitted by that complete theory.

novelty.explanation: It develops the identity response without claiming that identity alone explains every normative dimension.

premises.text: Epistemic conceivability can reveal ignorance without establishing a probability space, and neither numerous scenarios nor intuitive simplicity determines their relative weight under naturalism.

novelty.explanation: It preserves the conceivability insight while denying the unsupported inference from possibility to probabilistic weight.

premises.text: A theistic likelihood also requires an account of divine choice among many valuable worlds, including worlds with different embodiments, tradeoffs, limitations, and distributions of suffering.

novelty.explanation: It strengthens the comparative objection by applying underdetermination to the theistic side as well as naturalism.

premises.text: Complete packages should therefore be compared using explicit commitments, explanatory derivations, simplicity costs, and fit, with any local harmony likelihood derived from rather than substituted for that analysis.

novelty.explanation: It operationalizes the complete-theory reframe and accommodates consciousness theories that crosscut theological categories.

conclusion.text: Until the datum and comparison class are fixed and both likelihoods receive theory-relative grounding, psychophysical harmony supplies no established comparative shift toward theism, although future complete theories could alter that assessment.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion replaces certainty with a burden-based result that remains open to better specified theoretical accounts.

newArguments.title: Datum-sensitivity test
newArguments.text: Vary the definition of harmony before assigning evidential force. If harmony means phenomenal-neural coinstantiation, identity theory predicts it trivially. If it means adaptive functional organization, evolutionary and learning explanations become relevant. If it means objective normative appropriateness, a separate metaethical theory is required. If it means the production of valuable agency, both divine-choice and naturalistic realization questions arise. Because these formulations recruit different auxiliaries, treating them as one datum risks moving explanatory advantages between levels. A stable comparison should report results separately for each formulation.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new sensitivity analysis that decomposes harmony and tests whether conclusions survive alternative datum specifications.

newArguments.title: Symmetric underdetermination audit
newArguments.text: Apply the same underdetermination standard to both hypotheses. Naturalism requires a principled account of which consciousness theory and psychophysical structure it includes; theism requires a principled account of divine aims, permitted tradeoffs, embodiment choices, and world selection. Adding conceivable naturalistic mappings lowers a likelihood only if they receive weight, while adding valuable theistic worlds raises no specific likelihood unless divine preferences discriminate among them. A symmetric audit therefore withholds comparative support whenever either side's auxiliaries remain unspecified, preventing selective precision from deciding the result.

novelty.explanation: This is a new symmetry constraint applying equivalent auxiliary-hypothesis discipline to naturalistic and theistic likelihoods.
